effects: The signer sends msg.value in native ETH to the bundler.
The bundler calls MultiSourceLoan.multicall(executionData) and opens a loan (emitLoan): the lender's principal (WETH) goes to the bundler, and the signer, as borrower, owes principal plus interest.
In the afterPrincipalTransfer callback, when the purchase currency is an ERC20, the bundler pulls purchaseBundlerExecutionInfo.amount of it from loan.borrower (the signer).
The bundler can swap the principal on the Uniswap router and then buys the NFT on a whitelisted marketplace, using executionInfo.value and the module and data from the callback data.
A buy tax (taxes[module].buyTax of the purchase amount) goes to the protocol fee recipient out of the funds the bundler holds.
The NFT goes to the borrower, and MultiSourceLoan locks it as collateral for the new loan.
The bundler sends the leftover purchase currency and principal currency to the borrower, and the leftover ETH to msg.sender.
formats.shown: "Buy NFT with a loan", the ETH value sent, and a nested Gondi "Borrow against NFT" screen with collateral, lender, principal, APR, duration and the purchase instructions as raw callback hex.

findings.title: buy: the purchase price, marketplace and ERC20 amount taken from the signer exist only as raw callback hex.
findings.evidence: PurchaseBundler._afterPrincipalTransfer: `ERC20(purchaseBundlerExecutionInfo.purchaseCurrency).safeTransferFrom(_loan.borrower, address(this), purchaseBundlerExecutionInfo.amount);` and `executionInfo.module.call{value: executionInfo.value}(executionInfo.data)`. Case 0 shows these only inside the nested field 'Callback data' as a 0x000…0020… hex blob.
findings.fix: No field path in this descriptor reaches the inner ExecutionInfo struct. Add a notice to the intent, e.g. 'Buy NFT with a loan (price set in loan data)', or ask for nested decoding of the MultiSourceLoan callback data.

findings.title: buy: the buy tax sent to the protocol fee recipient is not shown.
findings.evidence: PurchaseBundler._afterPrincipalTransfer: `_handleProtocolFee(_loan.borrower, purchaseAmount, address(purchaseCurrency), _taxes[executionInfo.module].buyTax);` The rate is in storage. No field mentions a fee.

findings.title: buy: the interpolated intent repeats the intent and names no NFT, price or debt.
findings.evidence: descriptor buy format: "interpolatedIntent": "Buy NFT with a loan". The NFT (Hoodnanas #3374) and the 0.0001 WETH debt appear only in the nested Loan screen of case 0.
findings.fix: Change the intent to say a debt is created, e.g. 'Buy NFT; it is locked as loan collateral'. The outer bytes[] arguments cannot feed the sentence.

effects: The bundler calls MultiSourceLoan.multicall(executionData) with repayLoan, and MultiSourceLoan releases the collateral NFT to the borrower.
In the afterNFTTransfer callback the bundler sells the NFT on a whitelisted marketplace. When contractMustBeOwner is set, it first pulls the NFT from the borrower with transferFrom.
A sell tax (taxes[module].sellTax of the sale proceeds) goes to the protocol fee recipient.
The bundler can swap the proceeds into the loan currency on the Uniswap router, using swapData. A price-quoter slippage check applies.
The bundler sends the sale proceeds or swap output to the borrower. MultiSourceLoan then takes the repayment (principal plus interest) from the borrower.
If the bundler still holds the NFT at the end, it sends it to msg.sender.
formats.shown: "Sell collateral and repay", a nested "Repay loan" screen (loan ID, collateral, principal, borrower, lender, raw callback data) and the raw swap bytes.

findings.title: sell: the sale price, buyer and marketplace of the collateral exist only as raw callback bytes.
findings.evidence: PurchaseBundler._afterNFTTransfer / _sellReleasedCollateralInMarketplace: `collateral.transferFrom(loan.borrower, address(this), tokenId); collateral.approve(executionInfo.module, tokenId); executionInfo.module.call{value: executionInfo.value}(executionInfo.data)`. Case 1 shows only 'Callback data' in the nested Repay loan screen.
findings.fix: No path in this descriptor can decode the nested ExecutionInfo. State in the intent that the sale terms are in the loan data.

findings.title: sell: Swap data is shown as raw bytes, and it decides what the sale proceeds become.
findings.evidence: descriptor sell format: {"path": "swapData.[]", "label": "Swap data", "format": "raw"}. Code: PurchaseBundler._swapAndCheck runs `_uniswapRouter.call{value: swapValue}(swapData)` and then `ERC20(loanCurrency).safeTransfer(loan.borrower, loanCurrencyBalance)`.
findings.fix: Hide the raw bytes, or give them a label that says what they do, e.g. 'Swap of sale proceeds (router data)'.

findings.title: sell: the sell tax and the repayment amount (principal plus interest) are not shown.
findings.evidence: PurchaseBundler._afterNFTTransfer: `_handleProtocolFee(loan.borrower, saleAmount, ..., _taxes[executionInfo.module].sellTax)`. The nested screen of case 1 shows 'Loan principal 0.0001 WETH' but not the interest owed, which MultiSourceLoan computes.

formats.key: executeSell(address[] currencies, uint256[] currencyAmounts, address[] collections, uint256[] tokenIds, address marketPlace, bytes[] executionData, bytes[] swapData)
effects: The bundler pulls currencyAmounts[i] (minus its own balance) of each ERC20 currency from the signer. For ETH, the amount must already be in msg.value.
The signer sends msg.value in native ETH.
The bundler repays the seller's loan through MultiSourceLoan.repayLoan. In the callback it executes the borrower's marketplace listing and pays it with the signer's funds.
After the sale, leftover loan currency, or the swap output plus the whole remaining purchase-currency balance, goes to the borrower and not to the signer.
The bundler sends any remaining funds in each listed currency back to the signer.
If the bundler holds the NFT tokenIds from collections, it sends the NFT to the signer. Otherwise the marketplace calldata decides where the NFT goes.
formats.shown: "Buy Hoodnanas #3374" with the NFT, the payment amount and token, the marketplace address, the nested Repay loan screen, raw swap data and the ETH value sent.

findings.title: executeSell: native value above the payment can go to the seller, not back to the signer.
findings.evidence: PurchaseBundler._afterNFTTransfer swap branch: `_sendCurrency(purchaseCurrency, loan.borrower, purchaseCurrencyBalance);` Here purchaseCurrencyBalance is the bundler's whole ETH balance, msg.value included. The screen shows 'Payment' and 'Value sent' as two separate fields, with no statement about the difference.
findings.fix: Label the value field 'Value sent (not refunded above payment)', or document that Value sent must equal Payment.

findings.title: executeSell: the NFT recipient comes from marketplace calldata hidden in the nested callback bytes.
findings.evidence: PurchaseBundler._givebackNFT: `if (collection.ownerOf(tokenId) == address(this)) collection.safeTransferFrom(address(this), _msgSender(), tokenId);` No check makes sure the signer receives the NFT. The marketplace call data sits in the 'Callback data' of the nested Repay loan screen.

findings.title: executeSell: the interpolated intent names the NFT but not the payment amount.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "interpolatedIntent": "Buy {tokenIds.[]}". Case 2 renders 'Buy Hoodnanas #3374', and the 0.00011 WETH payment appears only as a field.

findings.title: executeSell: Swap data is shown as raw bytes.
findings.fix: Hide the field or give it a label that says it converts the seller's proceeds.

formats.key: executeSellWithLoan(((address pool, address[] assets, uint256[] amounts) borrowArgs, (address[] currencies, uint256[] currencyAmounts, address[] collections, uint256[] tokenIds, address marketPlace, bytes[] executionData, bytes[] swapData) executeSellArgs, bytes[] loanExecutionData, address[] swapCurrencies, uint160[] swapAmounts, bytes[] swapData, bool unwrap) args)
effects: On this deployment the function always reverts: aaveAddressProvider is the zero address, so `_aaveAddressProvider.getPool()` fails. Nothing moves.
By design (on a deployment with Aave), the bundler takes a flash loan, runs executeSell with the signer as buyer and pulls the payment from the signer.
By design, it opens a new MultiSourceLoan loan for the signer with loanExecutionData, which locks the NFT as collateral.
By design, it pulls swapAmounts of swapCurrencies from the signer and swaps them on the Uniswap router.
By design, it pulls any shortfall on the flash loan principal plus premium from the signer, and sends any surplus to the signer.
formats.shown: "Buy Hoodnanas #3374 with a loan" with the payment, marketplace, the nested repayment and new-loan screens, a flash loan pool and amount, the unwrap flag, raw swap data and the ETH value sent.

findings.title: executeSellWithLoan: the function always reverts on chain 4663 because the Aave address provider is zero.
findings.evidence: meta.json constructor argument aaveAddressProvider = 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000. PurchaseBundler.executeSellWithLoan: `address aaveV3Pool = _aaveAddressProvider.getPool();`. Case 3 renders 'Flash loan pool 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'.
findings.fix: Remove this format from the 4663 descriptor, or note that the function is not available on this chain.

findings.title: executeSellWithLoan: the flash loan shortfall and premium taken from the signer have no field.
findings.evidence: PurchaseBundler.executeOperation: `if (balance < owed) { asset.safeTransferFrom(_buyer, address(this), owed - balance); }` with owed = amounts[i] + premiums[i]. The screen shows only 'Flash loan' as the borrowed amount. Unreachable on this deployment.
findings.fix: If the function is ever enabled, add a label such as 'Flash loan (you cover any shortfall and fee)'.

findings.title: executeSellWithLoan: the screen has 16 fields, with raw bytes and a raw boolean.
findings.evidence: descriptor: 'Swap data' raw twice, 'Unwrap WETH' raw, plus two nested loan screens. Case 3 shows 12 rendered rows and two raw callback blobs.
findings.fix: Hide the raw swap bytes, and show 'Unwrap WETH' with an enum or a label.
